By Me they fall--not thee! the stroke of death is dealt them now, Even as they show thus gallantly; My instrument art thou!

Ah! if in anger now Thou shouldst remember I did think Thee Friend, Speaking with easy speech, As men use each to each; Did call Thee "Krishna," "Prince," nor comprehend Thy hidden majesty, The might, the awe of Thee; Did, in my heedlessness, or in my love, On journey, or in jest, Or when we lay at rest, Sitting at council, straying in the grove, Alone, or in the throng, Do Thee, most Holy! wrong, Be Thy grace granted for that witless sin!
Who troubleth not his kind, And is not troubled by them; clear of wrath, Living too high for gladness, grief, or fear, That man I love!
I will to thee unfold Some portions of My Majesty, whose powers are manifold!
For Thou art, now I know, Father of all below, Of all above, of all the worlds within Guru of Gurus; more To reverence and adore Than all which is adorable and high!
Mothers each mortal form, Brahma conceives, And I am He that fathers, sending seed!
As father to a son, As friend to friend, as one Who loveth to his lover, turn Thy face In gentleness on me!

Whereof sweet "Soothfastness," by purity Living unsullied and enlightened, binds The sinless Soul to happiness and truth; And Passion, being kin to appetite, And breeding impulse and propensity, Binds the embodied Soul, O Kunti's Son!

Who, unto friend and foe Keeping an equal heart, with equal mind Bears shame and glory; with an equal peace Takes heat and cold, pleasure and pain; abides Quit of desires, hears praise or calumny In passionless restraint, unmoved by each; Linked by no ties to earth, steadfast in Me, That man I love!

[Hide, the holy Krishna saith, This from him that hath no faith, Him that worships not, nor seeks Wisdom's teaching when she speaks: Hide it from all men who mock; But, wherever, 'mid the flock Of My lovers, one shall teach This divinest, wisest, speech-- Teaching in the faith to bring Truth to them, and offering Of all honour unto Me-- Unto Brahma cometh he!
For he that laboureth right for love of Me Shall finally attain!
Yea! for its leaves Are green and waving hymns which whisper Truth!
He shall not fall in sin who fronts the task Set him by Nature's hand!
The very truth--Heart's Lord!--of Sannyas, Abstention; and enunciation, Lord!

Thus hath been opened thee This Truth of Truths, the Mystery more hid Than any secret mystery.

This friendly human frame, my mind can think Calm thoughts once more; my heart beats still again!
Undismayed Let me once more behold The form I loved of old, Thou of the thousand arms and countless eyes!
Sad is the steadfastness wherewith the fool Cleaves to his sloth, his sorrow, and his fears, His folly and despair.
Religion followed by a witless will To torture self, or come at power to hurt Another,--'tis of Tamas, dark and ill.
By this same love and worship doth he know Me as I am, how high and wonderful, And knowing, straightway enters into Me.
Learn from me, Son of Kunti! also this, How one, attaining perfect peace, attains BRAHM, the supreme, the highest height of all!
Moreover, when a soul departeth, fixed In Soothfastness, it goeth to the place-- Perfect and pure--of those that know all Truth.
What Thou hast said now know I to be truth, O Kesava! that neither gods nor men Nor demons comprehend Thy mystery Made manifest, Divinest!
